text:
A small first project
Put the analysis steps in _proj.yml:
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
build:
  scripts: [analysis.py]
These paths are explicit, not runtime defaults. The Python example uses cache; raw-data and output match the local setup preset. The tutorial explains their roles and local-only initialization.
Run the preview from your project folder:
proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
The step-by-step example supplies the script, a tiny dataset, and the result to check. It uses Python’s standard library.

title: Preview release delivery
text:
The reviewed pipeline prepares a draft prerelease for an existing vX.Y.Z-preview.N tag whose version exactly matches Cargo.toml. It does not bump versions, push commits, publish an APT repository, sign credentials or publish the draft automatically. No new release is implied by this documentation.
Remote locked tests/builds produce Linux x86-64 and Windows x86-64 binaries. Linux uses Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35 or newer); the initial user-local WSL installation target is Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64. macOS/ARM delivery is not verified or supplied by this pipeline. Each asset is named proj_<version>_<os>_<arch>[.exe], with matching version.txt and checksums.txt. Exact-tag help/version/protocol smokes and actual installer tests must pass before assets enter the draft. Checksums detect corruption and mismatches; they are not independent signatures or reproducible-build attestations.
Installers default to MiguelRodo/projcli, require version metadata and exactly one matching SHA256 entry, and verify downloaded bytes before replacement. They stage on the installation filesystem and need only an existing user-writable directory. PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION pins a release (with optional v); preview releases should always be pinned because GitHub’s latest URL normally selects stable releases. PROJ_INSTALL_DIR selects an existing absolute user directory without changing PATH or system settings. Existing older releases lacking the new metadata fail closed instead of installing an unverified fallback binary.
Before publication: reconcile reviewed supported behavior and limits, update the Cargo/Cargo.lock preview version in a reviewed change, verify required checks, then create the exact reviewed tag. Inspect the resulting draft assets/version/ checksums and retain disposable-project warnings. Publish only after those checks. For WSL, download the pinned binary/manifest, verify SHA256, preserve any existing user-local binary, install into the chosen user-local directory and smoke help, version, capabilities and a disposable configured preview. No local compilation, sudo, persistent authentication change or R package modification is needed.
Known limits include bounded captured-state recovery, arbitrary external script effects, incomplete direct R/IDE parity, incomplete attempt/release records and analysis-free publication retry. This is a development preview, not M2 completion.

title: proj path get
text:
Resolve a project resource independently of your current working directory.
proj path get --label <LABEL> [--target final|safe] [--format auto|absolute|relative] [--relative-to BASE] [--project <PATH>] [PART ...]


Ordinary labels must be declared in the active configuration with a nonempty path. ASCII case is ignored. Undeclared labels and suffixes are errors: declaring raw-data does not declare raw or raw-data-extra. Relative paths resolve against the captured project root; explicit external directories are allowed. Queries do not create directories. Safe lookup is the default and resolves generated output into the versioned cache. Use --target final for the configured released destination.



--project PATH selects that exact existing directory, including a folder without configuration or VERSION. It overrides both ancestor discovery and an inherited run root. Invalid directories fail with a nonzero exit status.
The CLI captures an absolute root as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT for the invocation and its child processes. A nested proj path get uses that root even after a script changes cwd. An invalid inherited root fails rather than falling back silently. Direct Rust build_project(root, ...) calls also pass their supplied root to children. See the discovery rules below for the recognized root markers.
This establishes CLI child-query behavior, not direct Quarto/RStudio parity or changes to the existing R frontend. Renderer configuration, execution cwd, resource links and output placement remain separate concerns. Path queries do not write ignore files or create the resolved target directories.



Without --project or an inherited run root, discovery walks upward from cwd and selects the first recognized directory. It does not search downward for projects. Recognized markers are VERSION, README.md, _quarto.yml, _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, Git/SVN metadata, a DESCRIPTION containing Package:, an RStudio .Rproj whose first line starts Version:, and a renv.lock with a Packages map.
pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml deliberately extend the projr marker set for Python/Julia. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone are not root markers. Standalone VERSION and README markers are retained, so a nested directory with one is the nearer project; explicit selection overrides it.
Marker recognition does not change shallow default script enumeration or prove that the corresponding language runner/frontend is implemented. Legacy config content handling is a separate compatibility change from recognizing its root.
If no recognized marker exists, discovery selects cwd. Discovery success does not mean a build is configured: the current product contract requires active root configuration and explicit used-directory mappings. Validation changes enforcing that newer contract are separate from this root-discovery slice.



--target safe maps declared output/docs-class labels to <selected-cache>/projr/v<active-version>/<exact-declared-label>. One explicit safe: true cache wins; otherwise eligible exact label cache wins, then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. The chosen label is captured for child queries. A release version has no dev suffix; dev cache keys use a hyphen, such as v1.2.3-4. Other roles retain their configured targets.
--target final addresses the explicitly configured destination, including an absolute external directory. The CLI defaults to safe; production promotion is a separate build step. Path queries do not promote anything.
Optional parts extend the selected role, for example:
proj path get --label output --target safe figures result.png
Queries do not create directories. Unknown labels, missing cache/version for safe lookup, absolute/drive-qualified parts and parent traversal fail clearly. Explicit directory mappings stay mandatory; output-model does not imply an output alias. Path representation and native execution cwd remain separate policies.



--format auto returns a caller-cwd-relative filesystem path in ordinary execution and an absolute target in an explicitly known managed render child. It never infers render context from a .qmd filename, project marker or cwd. absolute and relative override auto. Explicit --relative-to cwd|project|document|/absolute/base requires relative format; document requires an individually known render document. Project renders without a single document reject that base. A custom base must be absolute.
Strict relative conversion fails across roots/drives. Auto ordinary execution falls back to absolute when no relative path exists; the absolute target stays identical. The CLI defaults to safe targets and auto representation. Merged settings.path-representation may select auto/absolute/relative; an explicit --format overrides it. The default is frozen with managed child context, while relative paths are expressed against each query caller’s current cwd. Getters create no directories.
Renderer descriptors are private per-command snapshots created only when launching Quarto/rmarkdown/Bookdown, alongside unchanged root/profile/version/mapping inputs. Ordinary scripts and dependency probes keep ordinary context. Existing R helpers do not consume this descriptor; direct IDE rendering does not gain automatic parity. Absolute results are filesystem targets, not literal Markdown/LaTeX URL rewrites.



proj path get --label output-r-data --target final
proj path get --label output-r-data result.rda
The first returns project/data even without YAML; the second derives a safe target from the selected declared cache and active version. Neither creates directories nor activates cleanup, recovery, promotion or publication of package data. Explicitly declare directories.output-r-data: {} to activate ordinary output management. Legacy _projr data declarations normalize before merging. Its final destination cannot be redirected. There is no special preservation policy: configured pre/post clearing applies normally; preview never promotes.
Built-in project lookup returns the selected root. No Python, Julia or inst role is introduced; use ordinary output mappings or proj path get –label project inst for a root-relative fragment.

title: proj ignore
text:
Commands for interacting with tracking file exclusions, handling operations to manually or automatically modify .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.


Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.
Unlike automatic configurations driven by _proj.yml, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly above the # --- PROJ MANAGED --- blocks.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
--force-create: Boolean flag (default true). If true, creates ignore files if they don’t exist. If false, skips file creation unless inherently warranted by environmental cues (e.g. finding a .git folder or a DESCRIPTION file).
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the manual path entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. !path/ or ^!pattern$).
These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly below the # --- END PROJ MANAGED --- boundary in .gitignore and .Rbuildignore files.



<PATHS>...: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
--type: Optional filter selection (all [default], git, rbuild). Determines which tracking surface receives the negated entries. Note that .Rbuildignore is skipped entirely if no DESCRIPTION file exists at the project root.





The library core automatically synchronizes ignore rules dynamically across .gitignore and .Rbuildignore based on the configuration of _proj.yml.

Note: While the automated ignore synchronization is invoked implicitly by the CLI via commands like proj yml read (and acts seamlessly under the hood), the ignore subcommand namespace exists openly to support explicit manual additions via proj ignore add.




The tool automatically locates the project boundaries via a heuristic upward path traversal. It begins checking from the user’s current working directory upward: - It discovers the conceptual root by finding a directory containing a VERSION file. - It continues upward through up to 5 directory levels seeking an optimal foundational root confirming the presence of either _proj.yml or a .git tracking context alongside the VERSION.



The tool targets specifically two core exception list files: - .gitignore (safeguards git commit environments) - .Rbuildignore (safeguards strict CRAN environments and rbuild processes)
Based on the individual block ignore settings within _proj.yml (e.g. ignore: all), properties are intelligently resolved as standard git glob patterns and Rbuild regex match patterns appropriately.



Modifications made by the tool into .gitignore and .Rbuildignore are safely strictly demarcated with protected slice logic block comments. This preserves user-defined modifications outside the managed span: - Operations scan for # --- PROJ MANAGED --- and # --- END PROJ MANAGED ---. - Targeted slice elements are swapped or appended into existing scopes only between these exact markers. - If the boundary blocks are absent, the tool automatically injects them natively at the base end.

title: proj version get
text:
Get the project version based on the VERSION file.


The command searches upwards from the current directory to discover the project root containing the VERSION file. It parses the version text (supporting both raw strings like v1.0.0 or JSON objects) and resolves it to a standard output.
If the VERSION file is missing, the tool attempts to fall back and parse the version from an R package DESCRIPTION file if one is present in the project root. If neither a VERSION file nor a DESCRIPTION file exists, it defaults to a newly initialized v0.0.1.
proj version get





Omits the ‘v’ prefix from the output string.
proj version get --no-v



Specifies the output format: - text (default): Outputs the version as a standard string identifier. - json: Outputs the version as a serialized JSON object, detailing its properties (major, minor, patch, and optionally dev).
proj version get --format json




When using --format=json, the output consists of the separated standard semantic components: - major (integer) - minor (integer) - patch (integer) - dev (integer, optional, indicating build cycles or pre-release versioning)

title: Future R wrapper: CLI installation and CRAN checks
text:
Status: design direction recorded on 2026-10-20, not a shipped wrapper or an accepted CRAN submission. The existing R package remains untouched. This note does not settle the complete frontend protocol or claim renderer parity.


The future wrapper is intended to contain R code that calls a separately installed proj CLI. Its DESCRIPTION should declare that CLI in SystemRequirements. It should discover a compatible executable and give an actionable missing/incompatible-CLI error. A user-invoked installer on the user’s own machine is distinct from automatic downloads during CRAN installation, checks or examples. Do not assume CRAN servers already provide proj.
CRAN source-package policy permits downloads of precompiled software only as a last resort with CRAN-team agreement. A separate executable is not an automatic exemption. Review Writing R Extensions: portability when implementing the package, including external software availability and portable invocation. This work has neither requested nor obtained CRAN agreement; no outreach is authorized here.










Environment
Required behavior




CRAN, CLI absent
Always run meaningful R-only validation, argument construction, missing-CLI diagnostics and mocked protocol/response tests. Skip only genuine executable integration tests, explicitly because the CLI is unavailable.


CRAN, compatible CLI available
Run the applicable real integration tests as well as the R-only tests. Do not assume every check host supplies it.


Our integration CI
Install an exact pinned CLI release, verify its checksum and compatible version, and run real end-to-end tests. Missing CLI or failed installation is a failure, never a silent skip.



Mocked responses check the wrapper contract; they do not prove the CLI or renderer works. Our mandatory integration job supplies that evidence. Examples and vignettes must also handle optional executable availability honestly instead of requiring an undeclared download. A requirement to execute proj on CRAN check servers would need an agreed deployment/checking arrangement, not an assumed policy exception.



The pinned Quarto R package DESCRIPTION at v1.5.1 declares the separate Quarto command-line tool in SystemRequirements. Its test helper can skip executable-dependent tests when Quarto is unavailable, and its vignette utility checks executable availability during vignette processing. These are specific implementation precedents, not proof that CRAN has accepted a future proj wrapper or guaranteed an executable on every server. This note does not infer automatic binary-download permission from Quarto’s existence.
Before implementation, specify compatible protocol versions, executable discovery, argument quoting, diagnostics, and which tests are unconditional versus executable integration. R production changes require separate authorization.

Preview feature status
The published development release is 0.4.0-preview.2. The verified WSL user-local command also reports that version. See release evidence for the exact source and checks.
This is an early Rust CLI for disposable analysis projects. A development preview does not mean the complete roadmap is finished. Use independent backups and sample data while evaluating it. The existing projr R package and thesis remain unchanged.



Area
Available Rust behavior
Verification and limits




Project selection
Explicit root; nearest recognized ancestor; markerless cwd fallback; shallow default script discovery.
Cross-platform fixtures cover markers, nested invocation and explicit override. Root recognition includes Python/Julia markers; that does not imply Julia execution or a wrapper.


Configuration and init
Active root YAML required; legacy alias/ambiguity rule; profile precedence; explicitly declared resource directories; local-only directory initialization.
Cross-platform configuration/error-preservation fixtures. Old no-config roadmap assumptions were superseded.


Execution context
Ordered explicit scripts/hooks; native cwd with explicit project-root override; supported Quarto/R Markdown root controls; unsafe/unknown layouts fail early.
Real Python/R/rendering acceptance and cross-platform fixtures passed. Direct R API/IDE parity remains unproved.


Automation
Opt-in protocol-v1 JSON, capability version, typed queries, noninteractive command worker, nonzero failures; child logs on stderr.
Cross-platform machine tests. Static coarse error codes; no invented attempt/release record on success.


Preview preservation
The released CLI restores captured managed state after successful/failed previews. Cache results remain.
Included through the reviewed recovery dependency; final integrated tests and actual released-binary checks passed. Generated-output path queries use the safe cache by default; arbitrary writes are not isolated.


Production safety groundwork
Path guards, bounded local failure recovery, optional checked Git publication and verified CAS bytes.
Focused fixtures and reviews; incomplete release identity/provenance/retry model. This page is not an invitation to run on valuable production data.


Binary delivery
Development prerelease 0.4.0-preview.2 supplies versioned Linux/Windows x86-64 assets with mandatory checksums.
Exact-tag workflow, uploaded/public asset hashes and both native binary smokes passed. WSL user-local installation and tiny success/failure Python previews passed. Other platforms are not supplied.



Still unfinished: direct projr/quarto R API/RStudio parity, existing R helper integration, automatic isolation of every script write, durable attempt/release identifiers, complete input/code/config/dependency provenance, multi-writer/crash atomicity and analysis-free publication retry. Capture/recovery cannot undo arbitrary external script effects or guarantee concurrent readers never observe temporary changes. User/third-party logs are not automatically secret-redacted.
M1 is delivered as the useful local CLI preview in 0.4.0-preview.2. It requires active root configuration; initialization is optional. Explicit file-based R/Python/report steps, captured context, inspectable cached results and honest structured failures work without Git credentials. Supported previews preserve recorded final/archive/version state on success and failure. Runtime path guards and preflight remain essential; arbitrary child code is not sandboxed.
General command/argv forms, stronger process confinement and broader maintenance audits remain follow-ups. M2 records/provenance/retry and later frontend work are not completed by M1. See delivery boundaries, behavior and the compatibility log for supported details and remaining gaps.

title: projr compatibility and change log
text:
The behavior contract owns current product decisions. This log records comparison evidence, implementation differences and gaps. Update it in every focused PR; do not infer runtime parity from similar source or green Rust CI.
Relationship labels are same, different, new, and unverified. Each entry states whether that label concerns documented intent, static source, or executed behavior. No comparative R runtime tests have been run for the entries below. Local R/Docker workloads have not been run.



R baseline: SATVILab/projr at 3ac2959.
Thesis baseline: design at b110da5.
Rust pre-migration baseline: 024589b.

New comparisons must pin source commits and relevant files, record the decision and rationale, link executed tests, and distinguish approved, implemented and unverified behavior. Changing a reference baseline does not silently change the product contract.




Relationship: unverified runtime parity; same documented intent. The R README and thesis design describe development previews separately from publication. This is evidence of intent, not proof that every R development path is inert.
Decision/rationale: keep CLI-managed release/version/archive changes out of previews so researchers can inspect development results without publishing.
Implemented: PR123, merged 5d145293e596c5797e9620bd3f00978fa6f99411; Dev-gated VERSION writes, cleanup, document promotion, local export and ignore updates in build.rs, env.rs and yml.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests, including test_preview_safety.rs, and installer checks passed on reviewed head 5d3ac227f52b33fd0c32fddd479cb7296c4072a5. A disposable installed-CLI Python fixture reproduced the previous version/output/ignore mutations.
Gaps: cooperating Python scripts only; renderer YAML rewriting, automatic output isolation, repeated runs, same-project concurrency and full production lifecycle behavior were not established. Subprocesses are not a sandbox.





Relationship: new explicit contract; renderer parity unverified. R path.R dynamically discovers a root, while the thesis defines the project workflow.
Decision/rationale: current approved behavior supersedes defects and stale architecture claims. Root/path defaults must agree across projr, quarto::quarto_render() and RStudio QMD Render. Quarto root equals proj root; nested Quarto projects are unsupported. Direct rendering does not imply release lifecycle parity; R Markdown Knit is a separate entrypoint.
Implemented: PR124, merged 635aa9efac0d7a28971236ab78c879b21be5ec31, corrected AGENTS/README/flow guidance and added the behavior contract. This was documentation, not renderer code.
Executed evidence: independent document review and remote Rust CI passed at dbf8d5fd94a87bba32ffc95cd2ee3b47f1e04277.
Gaps: no direct R frontend, Quarto/RStudio GUI or fresh-render-session parity test was performed. No projr production code or thesis text was changed.





Relationship: different root-resolution mechanism; new CLI selection. R path.R calls root discovery from current context. The CLI now captures one absolute root and passes it to each managed child as PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT.
Decision/rationale: explicit selection wins, and path queries must not change projects after cwd changes. This deliberately improves unstable root behavior rather than copying it.
Implemented: PR125, merged f265eb46c91a300fe0aafad3119d998038946a0b; project.rs, ignore.rs, main.rs and build.rs. Direct library builds configure each child command instead of mutating the caller’s process-global root.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at 779b3010040eeb23f08434478e0812173eb2a723 cover explicit precedence, spaces, invalid roots, changed cwd and overlapping builds in two distinct roots.
Gaps: marker discovery was not changed; R path helpers and direct render entrypoints do not yet consume this captured context. The tests do not promise general environment isolation or same-project concurrent builds.





Relationship: same static read-only configuration intent; runtime R parity unverified. R yml.R reads/merges configuration; this does not establish equivalence of every R public path helper or its cache routing.
Decision/rationale: reading configuration or paths must not update ignore files. Mutating build/init operations request synchronization explicitly, and bad configuration must not replace custom ignores with default rules.
Implemented: PR126, merged cd34c3208f1ed1c3c27571e7ce2828498a4aecdb; yml.rs, build.rs, init.rs/main.rs.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at cc132f1e1b288c7560ff6b6b06fcac369a475355 snapshot files/directories for CLI queries, exercise direct API reads and production ignore synchronization, and preserve custom ignores on malformed/read-failing config. Permission-denied coverage ran on Linux/macOS.
Gaps: supported aliases, unknown-option handling and effective merged script/hook configuration remained unchanged and incomplete.





Relationship: new CLI transport contract; same failure-reporting intent. R build-engine.R uses R errors; that is not a process exit-code protocol for language wrappers.
Decision/rationale: a printed error must not be returned as successful execution. Failed Git remote inspection must not proceed to GitHub creation.
Implemented: PR127, merged 8e955b32bc1f611d38a8931d489de2bdfc50d5c7; main.rs routes operation failures to nonzero status and init.rs propagates previously swallowed external failures.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests at a741b5f9de63dcb96ca527607105e5547be1da7c cover failing queries/version/init/ ignores, missing executables, child failure and successful queries. Local fake Git/GitHub commands on Linux/macOS made no network requests.
Gaps: structured error/capability protocols and clean/idempotent Git-init coverage remained open; failure status is not rollback or R-runtime parity.





Relationship: new CLI mode. The R baseline’s build-engine.R calls dependency helpers; no equivalent explicit CLI flag/parity is claimed.
Decision/rationale: machine invocations must not need the CLI’s prompts or automatic package installation. Controlled child stdin must actually be closed.
Implemented: PR128, merged f7ff7e92451a3174d6cb9c5fd60151621e66bd04 after independent review at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1; adds the flag, inherited mode, runner stdin closure and controlled R-probe stdin closure.
Executed evidence: three-platform tests and installer checks passed at that head; fake-R EOF/no-install tests ran on Linux/macOS and Python runner-stdin coverage ran on all three platforms.
Gaps: no actual R startup/renderer execution comparison; initialization retains existing requested-operation defaults and third-party code can ignore EOF. This does not establish general subprocess isolation.





Relationship: same absent-dev fallback; different explicit-empty guarantee. R yml-scripts.R falls back when dev scripts are absent. Empty-list behavior also passes through validation and renderer selection, so a reliable R upload-only no-analysis contract has not been demonstrated.
Decision/rationale: explicit [] selects no analysis, preserving hooks and production upload/export; absence still falls back. It must not discover or render unrequested files. Cleanup/promotion must preserve upload inputs.
Implementation status: PR129 removes the Dev-empty error and derives one analysis-selection guard for renderer setup/cleanup/promotion. tests/test_empty_scripts.rs checks hooks, existing output/docs bytes, actual production archive bytes and preview nonpublication.
Executed evidence: three-platform Rust tests and installer checks passed at f4b3739554dc548911019c450ca1e90a196d33d2; independent review inspected those logs and cleared that code head. The documentation-only final head 999b730fd2cc23215e4a07a1231d7d6fa3543966 passed all nine checks in runs 39486028024/39486028097 and independent review. Merged as 5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb; post-merge test, installer and site runs 39486858711/39486858532/39486858701 passed.
Gaps: YAML null-as-absence and malformed-list validation were inspected in source, not newly exercised by this policy slice. No R runtime empty-list parity test or real renderer execution is claimed.
Confirmed but separate runtime gaps: retain projr markers (including README/ VERSION), accept legacy _projr.yml with a both-base-files error, and use local > profiles > base with earlier profiles first. The R precedence evidence is yml.R. These approvals are recorded in the behavior contract; this change does not implement aliases, marker expansion or merged script/hook context.




The actual .agents/skills/ponytail/SKILL.md is vendored unchanged from DietrichGebert/ponytail v4.10.0, upstream commit e3ba2aa6f1e6f0bc4d69eb09c9f0d0a93af56156, as installed by PR121. Its pinned upstream bytes and the existing projcli, projr, setupmjr and projects copies all have SHA-256 1316a2f3f95741d2300b116fe0c2d81ce4a9568656ed0a62643f54aaf09957f2. The established setupmjr vendoring contract matches; no duplicate or replacement skill was installed.
The skill prescribes the full-mode simplicity ladder, tracing callers before changing shared behavior, reusing existing code/stdlib/dependencies, and leaving an appropriate runnable check. It supplies no separate executable review script. Applying that guidance is a self-review, separate from independent review and CI.
Completed-chunk review of PR128 at 5dedee7da69cbe52837993e86bc4837c4c3342a1:

Traced the prompt helpers, main description prompt, dependency probes, install branch, script/hooks and project-render runners. Reused the existing EnvGuard, one shared mode predicate and standard-library null stdin; no dependency or custom execution framework was introduced.
Finding/action: the R package probe also needed closed stdin before package detection. That path was corrected and covered by a live-input/fake-R EOF test. Rechecking all controlled status/output paths found no further necessary change.
All three remote Rust suites and installers passed; this self-review remained separate from the independent exact-head review.

Completed-chunk review of PR129’s empty-selection change:

Reused the existing explicit-list resolver and pipeline; no new execution framework, configuration key or dependency was added.
Traced preflight, version, cleanup, hooks, document promotion and publication. Finding: skipping script execution alone could still erase upload-only inputs or require unused renderers. Action: derive one shared analysis-selection guard and apply it before those stages; keep hooks/publication outside that guard.
Retained data-preservation and failure handling. Added runnable integration checks for real archive bytes and absence-versus-empty semantics; those checks passed on all three remote platforms at the code head recorded above. No R runtime parity was inferred.





Relationship: same static projr marker intent; deliberate extensions. projr path.R at 3ac2959 combines VCS, VERSION, README, R-package, RStudio, renv and Quarto criteria. Exact structured-marker patterns were checked in rprojroot root.R at 4d2f450.
Decision/rationale: retain those markers with nearest-wins; remove Rust’s VERSION-first/five-extra-ancestors heuristic. Add pyproject.toml and Julia Project.toml/JuliaProject.toml as requested language extensions. Proj config files also anchor a configured project without VERSION. Requirements/orphan manifests do not create roots. Explicit selection still wins.
Implementation/evidence status: root_from now tests each ancestor once, never child projects. tests/test_root_markers.rs covers retained marker patterns, invalid structured markers, weak/nested markers, deep invocation, explicit override and a configured Python preview with shallow enumeration. At code head a0d459c5b3a31437443832436535b70d34838553, all nine checks passed in runs 39487247962/39487247928. Independent review compared the pinned marker sources and inspected all three platform logs, clearing that head. Symlink normalization was source-inspected, without a new dedicated test. Final evidence-only head 55e5606e7916f78de7dfb03a4bb43b0ae1a87987 passed all nine checks in runs 39487685152/39487685131 and independent review; merged as 41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1. No R-runtime parity is claimed.
Gaps: required active config, explicit used-directory mappings, early unsupported-setting validation, legacy config-content aliases and full frontend/renderer parity are separate changes. A marker does not claim a Julia runner exists.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused the public root_from entrypoint, existing regex dependency and standard filesystem APIs, replacing the old special-case traversal instead of adding a discovery framework. Traced explicit/inherited precedence and all root callers. Kept discovery read-only and shallow, with runnable positive/negative predicates and workflow coverage; no new dependency.





Relationship: different from prior convenience-default assumptions. The initial Rust/projr-style defaults and historical no-config fixtures are no longer the target behavior. Builds require active root-level configuration and explicit used-directory mappings; init may write familiar defaults into that file, but runtime must not invent missing directories or unknown subpaths.
Decision status: approved. The agreed _proj.yml / legacy _projr.yml names apply; explicitly activated profile files may provide configuration, while inactive profiles alone do not satisfy the requirement. Cwd discovery fallback does not waive build validation. Unknown behavior-affecting settings must fail before mutation.
Failure/publication target: restore pre-build state except permitted cache residue; storage/publication retry must not rerun or mislabel analysis. Existing staging/version/publication behavior does not yet prove that transaction.
Evidence/gaps: earlier CI entries remain accurate historical evidence for their source commits, not acceptance of the superseded no-config/default-path policy. Future fixtures must declare used paths and active configuration. The current core still needs enforcement and failure tests for the new rules.
Authorship boundary: the existing R package is entirely off limits, including root-helper fixes. A later backend port/integration must establish R parity; no such work or runtime comparison is claimed here. Thesis text remains untouched.





Relationship: same projr local > profiles > base precedence, with earlier-listed profiles winning; legacy _projr.yml is accepted alongside canonical _proj.yml as an explicit compatibility decision. Both base files together fail instead of silently merging. Source comparison remains projr yml.R at 3ac2959.
Implemented: shared base selection for merged reads, existing build base inspection, parameters insertion and local-profile cloning. Explicit profile lists replace ambient lists; traversal-like explicit names fail validation. Profile/local files retain their existing _projr- names in this bounded slice.
Evidence: new runnable query/alias/ambiguity/preservation/precedence tests passed on all three platforms at 53463d325c85c538ae0b8a5e792caa6bc997e452. All nine checks in runs 39488461110/39488461213 passed; independent review inspected alias, precedence and duplicate-key logs and cleared that head. Final documentation/instruction head c8b208f9243f828de05977f8e76d6f2074535a9b passed all nine checks in runs 39489639669/39489639654 and independent review; merged as 0fec2735355ee5e9b9ba64d33ecd4796bf396301. Post-merge checks passed. No R runtime tests.
Gaps: one merged build script/hook context, active-configuration requirement, explicit directory mappings and early unsupported-setting validation remain separate work. This does not claim builds yet satisfy those approved rules.
Ponytail full-mode review: traced base filename readers and reused one stdlib path selector; reversed existing deep-merge traversal rather than adding a merger or dependency. Preserved null-as-absence and explicit-empty-list behavior. Checks exercise real query results and preservation on ambiguity.

PR131 failure-path review found that direct YAML-to-JSON deserialization allowed duplicate keys to overwrite earlier values. Restored YAML Value parsing before JSON conversion, preserving duplicate-key rejection at every active layer. Added top-level and nested duplicate-key regressions for both base filenames, profile and local files, including CLI failure before preview state writes. The prior green CI did not cover this malformed-input case; the corrected head above passed the new checks and independent re-review. Ponytail review kept this at the shared file parser rather than guarding individual callers.




Relationship: new/unverified design. The durable CRAN note records the discussed future R-code wrapper around a separately installed CLI, meaningful unconditional R-only/mocked tests, conditional executable integration on CRAN, and mandatory pinned/checksummed CLI integration in our own CI. It cites current policy and pinned Quarto precedent.
No existing R code or tests were changed; no CRAN submission, agreement, preinstalled executable, automatic-download exemption or renderer parity is claimed. Implementation and runtime validation remain future work.
Ponytail full-mode design review: kept one linked design note; reused the repository’s behavior/compatibility/AGENTS pointers. No installer, wrapper, binding, mock framework or external contact was added speculatively.





Relationship: follows projr’s merged-configuration intent and the approved local > earlier profiles > later profiles > base precedence. The prior Rust pipeline validated merged settings but separately reread the base for execution.
Implemented: deserialize and validate one merged value, then select scripts and hooks from it. Explicit empty dev selection remains empty; absence falls back to build settings. Both base filenames use this same execution path. Configuration parsing/validation, target resolution and preflight now precede production environment-ignore writes.
Evidence: runnable Python fixtures check conflicting profiles, legacy base, local dev overrides and hook results, plus invalid merged configuration with a local environment file and missing-target failures leaving ignores/version/cache untouched. Remote CI and independent review pending; no real R/renderer execution is claimed.
Gaps: required active config, explicit mappings, all unsupported-field rejection and transactional rollback remain separate approved work. Environment loading still uses the existing process-global guard; this change makes no new same-process concurrent environment guarantee.
Ponytail full-mode review: removed the second base-only YAML parser and its ignored parse failure instead of adding a second configuration model. Reused existing typed validation and dev fallback rules. Traced validation, selection, hooks and environment-ignore writes; retained explicit error propagation.




The 2026-10-20 static audit records the pinned baseline, reported failure paths, required regressions and correction order. Its findings are not runtime reproductions or completed fixes. Highest managed-state risks remain blockers to production-safety claims; arbitrary external script effects are outside managed rollback. No mechanical edition upgrade or CAS redesign is claimed. This review uses the actual Ponytail full-mode skill to prioritize root causes and data-preservation checks over cosmetic rewriting.




Relationship: deliberate difference from projr convenience defaults, as explicitly approved. Every build requires a base file or activated profile; inactive profile/local files alone do not qualify. Discovery still falls back to cwd independently. Empty analysis is valid with active configuration.
Implemented: build gate before writes; unsupported typed configuration fields fail instead of disappearing in a top-level filter. Build failures include their error causes so unsupported-field diagnostics name the field. Arbitrary parameter and metadata maps remain supported and parameter aliases reach validation.
Evidence: runnable tests cover active/base/legacy/inactive/local/no-config cases, unsupported nested keys, dynamic maps and no pre-build state writes. Remote CI/independent review pending. Explicit directory enforcement is still a separate gap; this does not yet establish transaction/promotion safety.
Ponytail full-mode review: reused Serde’s unknown-field validation and the existing active profile resolver; removed silent filtering from runtime reads. No new parser/schema/dependency. Kept the old public filter helper only for compatibility; runtime no longer uses it.

PR134 merged-context evidence: exact head 29b2bdfb564f3193a0e93eb43096f89f2691653a passed all nine checks in runs 39490264159/39490264169. Independent review inspected the three new regressions across platforms and cleared the bounded change. Merged as eb1204026e8809780fc783f27b0be7edf9b5033e. Preflight itself is not guaranteed read-only; environment/profile-source unification, per-run environment safety, strict directories and transaction/promotion safety remain open. This evidence is batched with the substantive active-configuration change to avoid an extra matrix.
PR135 review found mixed parameter aliases survived per-file parsing as separate keys and then conflicted at typed deserialization. Canonicalize the one accepted alias to parameters in the shared reader before merging. New fixtures cover all 64 base/profile/local alias combinations, earlier-profile precedence and retained nested values; same-file multiple aliases and YAML duplicate keys remain errors. Ponytail full-mode re-review kept the fix at the shared loader, without caller guards or a second merge model. Exact amended CI/re-review remain required.




Relationship: new safety checks, not a blanket ban on external resources. Before production analysis cleanup, reject root/ancestor destinations, staging and resource overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, label path separators and symlinked managed-write paths. Directory replacement also requires an existing source and disjoint destination before deleting bytes.
Evidence: runnable preservation fixtures cover root, ancestor, staging, raw/output overlaps, traversal labels, Unix symlink parents and low-level self/ancestor/nested/missing-source moves. Remote CI/review pending.
Limits: does not yet provide atomic promotion or complete rollback, protect against concurrent hostile filesystem replacement, undo user-script external effects or establish full CAS integrity. External disjoint paths remain valid.
Ponytail full-mode review: one stdlib identity resolver shared by build and promotion guards; trace all promotion callers, retain explicit errors instead of silently accepting missing source/read errors. No new dependency.

Path-guard Ponytail re-review traced the public cleanup helpers as well as build: direct clear_pre/clear_post now apply the shared destination checks, clear_old rejects symlinked staging parents, and traversal-bearing version components fail before cache deletion. Label separator validation lives in shared typed validation for all modes. Generic destructive move APIs require resolved parents and reject symlink aliases; positive direct-API fixtures canonicalize their temporary roots so macOS system temp aliases do not violate that explicit safety precondition. Added a direct-cleanup preservation fixture. This is not complete transactional restoration or a guarantee against concurrent filesystem replacement.
PR135 final evidence (batched with path guards): code head 3839173366e55cffa946ea0e2afe4757ae48e77d passed all alias/conflict regressions on three platforms and independent re-review. Base-update head abc62f966766915093351c00a6a1724a0d1b69da changed no executable/tests/Cargo code, preserved the published site, passed all ten checks in runs 39492001512/39492001479/39492001493 and focused independent review. Merged as a0909e413915847498e77669a3b669941dbfe3fe. Required active config and unsupported field rejection are implemented; explicit used-directory enforcement and finite control-value validation remain separate gaps.
PR137 independent review found that configured-root checks alone missed derived version/output cache leaves. Validate all actual cleanup bases before the first deletion, including configured-cache and legacy staging paths. Direct dev cleanup is now a true no-op. The same review traced individual document promotion and recursive copying: validate paths before creating directories or renaming files, require actual outputs, reject traversal/aliasing and prevalidate asset moves. The two duplicate individual-renderer helpers now reuse one guarded implementation. Added targeted direct-API regressions; amended remote CI/re-review are required. This does not yet fix build callers discarding promotion errors or provide full restoration/atomicity; those remain the following focused work.
The repaired PR137 guard prevalidates concrete generated-file/asset paths and both legacy/configured cache-derived leaves before VERSION/ignore writes, including dangling links. Individual and project promotion now resolve the configured docs destination rather than a root/docs fallback; Python-only builds do not clear unrelated docs. Unix fake-Quarto/fake-R CLI fixtures exercise the reported linked root/docs sentinel bypass and actual successful external promotion, without a real renderer installation. Direct helper tests remain cross-platform.
Project-render source safety is explicitly conservative: recognized source-like .qmd, .Rmd, .md and .ipynb files or links in managed cleanup trees cause an early error. This can reject generated Markdown there; it is not exact Quarto or Bookdown input discovery. Keep sources and managed destinations separate until a renderer-provided input plan is supported. Quarto’s documented project input types are described in Project Basics.
The prepared literal-root glob fix is included in PR137 because a metacharacter root otherwise hides explicit inputs from the cleanup containment guard. Reuse glob::Pattern::escape for the root prefix only, retaining user include/exclude syntax. Runnable tests verify actual analysis bytes and selected-input preservation under a bracket-containing root. This is the same audited root-cause fix, not an additional discovery policy or dependency. Existing standalone preparation remains preserved and must not later be merged as duplicate work.
Windows CI at 9938173 exposed a skipped explicit failing script. Source review of glob 0.3.3 confirmed that escaping the canonical Windows namespace changes its filesystem prefix. Normalize Disk/UNC namespaces for glob transport only, keep filesystem prefixes literal, escape only directory components and join patterns using native path operations. The captured root is unchanged. Explicit include patterns with no files now fail instead of reporting successful no-op execution. New native/canonical-root execution markers run on every platform; network UNC execution remains unverified.
The same review found generated filenames could overwrite another selected script or hook, DESCRIPTION or environment configuration. Before renderer invocation, compare all concrete output/asset paths against the complete selected-input set and reject authoritative project/environment metadata filenames. Fake-renderer fixtures prove those failures happen before scripts, VERSION or ignore writes. Amended exact-head CI and independent re-review remain required.



Different (approved): runtime directory resolution requires declared nonempty paths and never invents missing labels or suffix subpaths. This supersedes earlier in-memory directory-default behavior, including read-only path queries. Missing configuration can still be queried as an empty inventory; builds require active configuration. Storage content labels must exist, and relative storage locations resolve against the captured root. Selected cleanup and project-render staging require cache; upload-only empty analysis does not require an unused cache mapping. Rendered documentation requires docs. Cache cleanup uses the declared mapping, not a parallel hard-coded _tmp tree.
Same preset / different timing: pinned projr 3ac29595d0e39552495d863661b99ea015d59d3d, R/yml-dir.R:334–345, supplies raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, output: _output. Rust local-only proj --project . --non-interactive init directories writes those explicit paths once when no base/active profile exists. Existing configuration stays byte-for-byte intact. No scripts field is generated: absence preserves discovery, while an existing explicit empty list stays empty. No Git/GitHub/R setup is invoked. The Rust accepted label-prefix subset still differs from projr’s broader labels; this slice does not claim full schema parity or R frontend changes.
Ponytail full-mode review reused the shared resolver and existing tempfile dependency rather than adding a directory framework. Existing malformed/unreadable config preservation tests remain; new tests cover missing paths, undeclared labels, case collisions, explicit storage references, cache ownership, no-executable local init, preserved base/legacy/profile bytes and actual default-discovered Python output. Remote CI and independent review are pending. Init is not an atomic transaction against filesystem failures or concurrent replacement.
PR137 final eb727912f2f0302d01611cca7b84188d34c34e82 independently cleared; all ten checks passed (runs 39496127892/39496127915/39496127894). Merge 56564b9a4aeeef03ae199b04140b5f3d325b3505 passed post-merge test and installation runs 39496869636/39496869586 and published the site in 39496869590.
Independent PR139 review removed an over-broad production cache prerequisite. Only selected operations that consume cache require its mapping. Explicit empty analysis can export declared existing results without cache/docs mappings. An explicit Python-only selection does not activate a renderer merely because its project marker exists. The custom-cache fixture now executes Python and checks actual custom staging cleanup plus preserved legacy _tmp bytes. Fake-R fixtures declare docs while retaining EOF/no-install assertions. These amendments require fresh remote checks and exact-head re-review.



Same precedence / deliberate error handling difference: inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles, then base assignments. Preserve non-Unicode inherited values rather than treating them as absent. Reject empty, equals-containing or NUL keys and NUL values before calling OS mutation APIs. Read whole files with propagated errors rather than lines().flatten(); required file errors and directory inputs cannot silently bypass validation or loop. Diagnostics include paths/line numbers, never assignment values. Same-file validation finishes before assignments from that file are applied. Ignore writes in explicit activation occur only after validation succeeds.
Ponytail full-mode review traced all load/assignment callers and reused existing configuration-entry presence checks. No parser dependency was added. Prepared CLI checks cover invalid/NUL entries, directory and permission-denied required files, secret-free diagnostics, actual inherited/local/profile/base child values and no analysis invocation on errors. This bounded fix does not make EnvGuard thread-safe: process-global environment mutation remains a known risk until per-run values and profiles reach all child commands and Git/preflight consumers. No project mapping is invented, and cache-free upload-only operations remain supported. Recovery sources are copied to temporary restore staging before any current target is removed. One local failure boundary covers ignore synchronization, cleanup, all pre/both/ post hooks, engine configuration, execution, output promotion and VERSION writing. After local success, storage export/Git publication form a separate failure phase: publication failure reports successful local analysis and retains the new local release. title: Run your first analysis
text:
1. Make a small project
In an Ubuntu terminal, choose a new folder and open it:
mkdir projcli-example
cd projcli-example
Create a file named _proj.yml with this content:
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: _raw_data
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output:
    path: _output
build:
  scripts: [analysis.py]
The paths are explicit: runtime does not supply missing mappings or invent undeclared labels.








Label
Folder
Role in this example




raw-data
_raw_data
Input files; unused because our three measurements are built into the script.


cache
_tmp
Temporary results; the script writes inside _tmp/preview.


output
_output
Result files; unused by this preview.



Only cache is used by this Python example. The other two mappings match the local initializer’s preset. No docs path is implied: document rendering needs an explicit docs mapping too.
The explicit build.scripts list selects our one script. No Git setup, remote repository or initialization command is needed for this manual setup.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
2. Add an analysis
Create analysis.py in the same folder:
import csv
import os
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

root = Path(os.environ["PROJ_PROJECT_ROOT"])
preview = root / "_tmp" / "preview"
preview.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

measurements = [10, 12, 14]
result = preview / "summary.csv"
with result.open("w", newline="") as handle:
    writer = csv.writer(handle)
    writer.writerow(["count", "mean"])
    writer.writerow([len(measurements), mean(measurements)])

print(f"Saved {result}")
The three measurements are deliberately built into the script so there is no data download or extra package installation. The script uses the project root provided by projcli and explicitly writes to _tmp/preview.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
3. Check, then run
proj --project . yml read
proj --project . --non-interactive build-dev
cat _tmp/preview/summary.csv
The CSV should contain:
count,mean
3,12
The validation command reads configuration. The preview runs the script. Running it again replaces this example’s CSV; change a measurement and rerun to see the mean change.

title: Run your first analysis
text:
4. Understand what changed
The script creates _tmp/preview/summary.csv. The CLI does not create a VERSION file, publish to docs, or export an archive during this preview.
A preview is not a sandbox: your script can still write elsewhere if you tell it to. Keep preview writes in an explicit temporary folder.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Ubuntu and WSL Ubuntu
Run this inside Ubuntu, not in a Windows terminal. Check that uname -m reports x86_64 and getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION reports glibc 2.35 or newer.
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
installer="$(mktemp)"
curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/768da1bf1b83be83b657b36219f299f37130ba03/install-local.sh" -o "$installer" &&
  PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION=0.4.0-preview.2 \
  PROJ_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" bash "$installer"
rm -f "$installer"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
hash -r
proj --version
Expected version: proj 0.4.0-preview.2.
The script comes from the reviewed source commit. It downloads the pinned Linux binary, checks its SHA256 against the release manifest, and installs it as ~/.local/bin/proj. It replaces an existing proj in that folder only after verification succeeds. No sudo or local compilation is involved.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Windows
Open PowerShell 7 (pwsh) as your normal user:
$installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".local\bin"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $installDir | Out-Null
$installer = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("proj-install-" + [guid]::NewGuid() + ".ps1")
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/768da1bf1b83be83b657b36219f299f37130ba03/install.ps1" -OutFile $installer
$env:PROJ_RELEASE_VERSION = "0.4.0-preview.2"
$env:PROJ_INSTALL_DIR = $installDir
& $installer
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $installer
$env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path"
proj --version
Expected version: proj 0.4.0-preview.2.
The script checks the Windows binary’s SHA256 before installing proj.exe in $HOME\.local\bin. It does not change system settings or require an administrator terminal. This installer is checked with PowerShell 7; these instructions do not claim Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility.

title: Install the development preview
text:
Finding the command later
The PATH lines above make the command available in the current terminal. In a new terminal, repeat that PATH line or add the installation folder to your own user PATH. The installer does not make that permanent change for you.
Another program can also be named proj. Check command -v proj in Ubuntu or Get-Command proj in PowerShell, then proj --version, if you see unexpected help or results.

title: Install the development preview
text:
What the checksum proves
The installer requires the release’s version.txt and exactly one matching entry in checksums.txt. A missing or incorrect checksum stops installation before the existing binary is replaced. For a manual download, use sha256sum on Linux or Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 in PowerShell and compare the result with the manifest’s exact filename entry before running it.
The manifest comes from the same GitHub release. Checksums detect corruption and mismatches; they are not independent signatures or proof of a reproducible build. The release also includes source-commit.txt and version.txt. The reviewed source is 768da1bf1b83be83b657b36219f299f37130ba03.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
This is the product behavior contract. Confirmed decisions below guide implementation; they are not claims that the current CLI already implements them. Proposals require review before they become requirements. The compatibility log records pinned projr comparisons, decisions, actual test evidence, Ponytail reviews and remaining gaps; update it with each PR.



A project is one analysis/build unit anchored at a selected root directory. It has settings, version information and named resource paths where applicable. Resource paths may be outside the root; a project need not be a Git repository.
Explicit project selection overrides discovery and selects that exact directory.
Automatic discovery walks upward from the invocation directory. The nearest recognized project root wins, including when projects are nested. Discovery does not search downward for projects.
Retain existing projr root markers, including standalone VERSION and README, VCS roots, R-package/RStudio/renv/Quarto project markers, and extend recognition for pyproject.toml, Project.toml and JuliaProject.toml. Proj configuration files _proj.yml / _projr.yml also identify a root. requirements.txt and Manifest.toml alone do not. Recognition must no longer require VERSION before considering the other markers.
_proj.yml is the primary base configuration. Accept _projr.yml as a legacy alias and fail clearly if both base files exist; do not silently merge them.
Configuration precedence follows projr: local overrides profiles, profiles override base, and earlier-listed profiles win conflicts with later ones.
Missing dev.scripts falls back to build.scripts. An explicit empty list in either selects no analysis scripts and never triggers fallback/discovery. Hooks still run; production version/publication/export behavior remains available for upload-only workflows. Development previews never publish. Analysis cleanup and promotion are skipped when no analysis is selected, preserving upload inputs.
With no recognized marker, discovery falls back to cwd. This does not waive build validation: builds require an active root-level proj configuration. The agreed _proj.yml / legacy _projr.yml names apply; explicitly activated profile files may supply configuration, but inactive profile files alone do not. No-config build assumptions from the initial roadmap are superseded.
Ordinary framework/resource directories used at runtime must be explicitly declared. Built-in project and R-package data lookup are bounded exceptions described below. Initialization may write familiar projr defaults into configuration; runtime must not synthesize missing directory mappings or unknown subpaths.
Unsupported behavior-affecting configuration fails before mutations.
Explicit script and hook patterns, including exclusions, must have valid glob syntax. Invalid exclusions must fail preflight rather than silently select unintended code. Valid exclusion-only lists may select no files; an empty list still disables analysis.
Failed supported builds must restore pre-build state except permitted cache residue. This is required behavior, not an implemented transaction guarantee.
Storage/publication retries must have an upload-only route without rerunning analysis or falsely recording a new analysis. Explicit-empty analysis supports hooks/publication, but full retry identity/transaction semantics are separate.
The existing R package is entirely off limits in this effort. Direct R frontend integration is later work; no existing helper changes or parity claims follow from these Rust changes.
Default script/document enumeration is shallow at the selected project root. Directory and entry inspection failures must be reported; they must not silently become an empty or incomplete selection. Only regular root files are enumerated; links are not followed, and hidden/Git-ignored regular scripts remain eligible. Subdirectory targets require explicit selection or renderer project configuration.
Native runner working-directory behavior is the default; provide an explicit project-root execution override. Rscript/Python inherit launch cwd, source() normally inherits caller cwd, and QMD/Rmd document execution has its own native defaults. Selecting a nested file does not redefine project identity.
Resolve logical role targets from captured root/config/profiles/run version. Safe output/data roles use declared versioned cache; configured final destinations are separate. Auto path representation is caller-relative ordinarily and absolute in explicitly supplied render context; explicit absolute/relative bases override.
Embedded HTML is the supported target. Default embedding only when effective settings are unspecified; preserve explicit/inherited false. Literal Markdown/ LaTeX retain native resource meaning. Linked portability is deferred.
The resolved root is captured for the run. Path helpers, including a future frontend’s projr_path_get(), resolve against that root even if a renderer or user script changes its working directory.
A supported Quarto project’s root must equal the proj root. Nested Quarto projects beneath that root are unsupported for now. Nested document files are distinct from nested Quarto projects.
QMD rendering through projr, quarto::quarto_render(), and RStudio QMD Render are a future frontend parity goal, outside the bounded Rust M1 completion gate. Evaluation-directory/root-helper parity is not currently established. R Markdown Knit is a distinct entrypoint and must be verified separately. Shared project configuration and direct-entry root resolution are required; CLI-only flags or a parent process environment cannot establish this parity.
Direct rendering does not imply the build, version, commit or archive/export side effects of a proj-managed build.
Renderer evaluation roots must use supported renderer controls. Setting only the parent process cwd is insufficient. Root identity and evaluation cwd remain separate concepts; document asset/reference resolution is not redefined here.

The project root is the analysis workspace’s top-level directory, not the user’s operating-system home directory. Resolving a named resource path is also distinct from changing cwd or selecting a new root.




Apply the base filename compatibility rule consistently to profile/local files. The effective proj profile-list source is now defined below; renderer-native profile settings are not silently rewritten.
Evaluate Quarto execute-dir and R Markdown knit_root_dir / knitr root.dir for root-relative execution. Define the shared persistent configuration and direct-entry initialization before broad renderer changes; do not add nested Quarto project support or rely only on flags passed by proj.
Frontend transport/bindings and remaining environment/YAML compatibility details must be explicit. Familiar projr directory defaults belong in init-generated configuration only; Rust’s _raw and synthesized raw/data runtime paths are not acceptable substitutes for undeclared directories.




The core root finder implements nearest-recognized-ancestor discovery without a VERSION prerequisite. Its marker tests cover the retained projr patterns and deliberate Python/Julia/proj-config extensions and cwd fallback. Builds now require active configuration and typed validation rejects unsupported fields. Explicit directory mappings are enforced without runtime path defaults; full failure restoration remains open; historical passing fixtures do not demonstrate those new requirements. Individual scripts currently start at project root; changing to native runner defaults with an explicit override is pending. Captured-root stability is implemented for core CLI child queries after cwd changes, including independent simultaneous roots; direct R frontend/renderer parity remains unimplemented. Base-file aliases and first-wins profile merging use one merged typed configuration for validation and build script/hook selection. Profile/local filenames retain their existing _projr- form for now. Explicit empty script selection now skips analysis while preserving hooks and production publication; its tests cover production archive bytes and preview nonpublication without invoking real renderers.
Verify nested projects, explicit selection, paths containing spaces, shallow default enumeration, explicit subdirectory scripts, changed cwd, and each supported renderer’s evaluation root. Compare the same nested QMD through projr, quarto::quarto_render(), and RStudio QMD Render; test R Markdown Knit separately. Reject a nested Quarto project clearly. Verify that direct rendering leaves proj-managed release/version/export state alone. Use tiny fixtures and remote CI where practical. Subprocess execution is not a security sandbox, and path hashes alone do not establish scientific correctness or a reproducible environment.



The R wrapper/CRAN design note records separate CLI installation, unconditional R-only tests, conditional CRAN executable tests and mandatory pinned/checksummed executable integration in our CI. It is future design, not a shipped wrapper, CRAN approval or automatic-download permission.



Production builds and direct cleanup helpers reject project-root/ancestor write destinations, resource/staging overlaps, selected-input containment, VCS metadata, path separators in labels and symlinked write destinations. Empty analysis still runs hooks and must validate managed destinations. Disjoint external resource paths remain supported. Generic directory moves require an existing source and disjoint destination with resolved parents; symlink aliases are rejected.
Project renderers are conservatively rejected when managed cleanup trees contain recognized source-like documents or linked entries; this is not exact renderer input discovery and can reject generated Markdown. Individual outputs must use portable leaf filenames and may not replace framework configuration/state. Concrete cache/output/asset paths are checked before VERSION or ignore writes. Literal project roots are escaped for explicit include/exclude globs so brackets in a root cannot hide selected inputs from safety checks.
These checks do not establish atomic promotion, full rollback, protection against concurrent filesystem replacement, or undo arbitrary external script effects.



The pinned legacy audit records unresolved safety and correctness findings and the regression evidence required before claiming fixes.
