Builds resolve one environment snapshot and pass it to their child commands and configuration-profile selection. Environment files do not mutate the parent process on this path. Inherited OS values win over local, earlier environment profiles and base assignments; explicit build profiles override inherited PROJR_PROFILE. The same values reach dependency probes, scripts/hooks/renderers and existing Git helpers. Direct public legacy EnvGuard APIs and CLI startup guards still mutate process state and are not concurrent environment APIs. This change does not approve credential injection policy or establish a sanitized/sandboxed environment.



Script and hook subprocesses inherit invocation cwd by default, retaining explicit selected input paths. Quarto and individual R Markdown retain native execution directory settings. Explicit --execution-dir project passes the captured root via supported renderer controls. Input/mode/root remain data arguments to fixed R code. This does not imply direct R/IDE parity or a changed resource URL policy. The existing R package remains untouched.
Nested Quarto project metadata is rejected for selected documents and conservatively scanned implicit source trees. Individual rendering models one document-local format: HTML, PDF, Word, or supported native presentation/EPUB variants. Unknown/multiple formats, inherited individual metadata, custom R Markdown output filenames, dynamic R Markdown runtime and document-rendering hooks fail before controlled writes. Project-render validation remains conservative fresh-tree validation, not a complete renderer output manifest. Unsupported layout rejection does not assert renderer parity.
clear_output accepts only pre, post, or never; directory ignore accepts all, git, rbuild (case-insensitive), or an empty list. Invalid values fail before analysis, ignore synchronization or cleanup, including direct cleanup APIs.



Ingestion requires an existing directory, disjoint from its CAS storage and project index. Reject linked/unsupported source entries, non-UTF-8 filenames and ambiguous logical paths; logical identities use slash-separated components and case-sensitive names. Digests are canonical 64-character lowercase hexadecimal BLAKE3 values. Copy and hash the same stream; verify existing objects before reuse. Publish complete objects/manifests without replacing conflicting content. Replace project index bytes through a same-directory temporary file, escaping CSV metadata fields.
Manifest inspection validates structure and manifest byte identity; file inspection also hashes referenced object bytes. This does not provide a stable snapshot across concurrent source changes, multi-writer serialization, power-loss durability or one transaction across remote manifest and project index. Failure may leave valid orphan objects or an unindexed complete manifest; errors propagate and old index bytes stay intact. No source file is modified by ingestion. Symlink-alias paths remain unsupported under the conservative path guards; callers should supply resolved physical paths.



Git commits, pushes and network/upstream checks default off even when Git metadata exists. Only the resolved configured actions execute. Commit-enabled builds require clean initial Git state to avoid sweeping in unrelated edits; no-op commits succeed. Push captures the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference before build writes. Missing upstream and unmodeled custom push-only routing fail early. Native authentication is the default. An explicit token-helper opt-in uses fixed host-scoped code and ephemeral environment data, never secret argv/source or persistent credentials. Local build success remains distinct from publication failure.



Preview captures managed root files/config/VERSION, selected inputs, declared output/docs trees, configured local publication stores and ordinary VCS metadata. Restore exact captured bytes/presence on both success and failure; restoration failure makes preview fail and reports retained recovery data when available. Declared cache is disposable and excluded from recovery; preview/cache artifacts remain there. No Git/publication operations execute in preview.
Recovery uses private temporary storage outside project cache. Unsafe linked or overlapping recovery paths fail before analysis; file-based/worktree VCS pointers are unsupported for this bounded metadata guarantee. This does not redirect arbitrary script writes, protect undeclared/external effects, prevent concurrent reads of temporary modifications, or provide sandbox/crash/concurrent-writer atomicity. New unmanaged files are not a whole-project snapshot. Automatic preview output isolation remains separate from post-run captured-state preservation.



Release/install plumbing must verify version-bound platform assets/checksums before replacement and use locked remote tests/builds. The pipeline creates a draft prerelease only; publication and user-local WSL binary installation follow explicit artifact verification. See delivery boundaries. No local source compilation or production-readiness claim follows from installer CI.



Opt-in --machine emits protocol-v1 results/errors on stdout, with capability version negotiation independent of project discovery. Static error codes avoid reflecting credentials/config/argv. Queries return typed values; other existing commands reuse the CLI through a noninteractive worker whose logs use stderr. See machine interface for supported shapes and limits. This is a transport boundary over existing anyhow errors, not a second domain-error overhaul.



One effective profile list is selected before config/environment reads: CLI, nonempty PROJR_PROFILE, nonempty QUARTO_PROFILE fallback, then base/local build.profile default. Earlier profiles still win; local config is highest. A profile’s own build.profile does not redirect an already selected run. Native QUARTO_PROFILE rendering settings remain distinct; no R helper bridge follows. The private per-run PROJ_RUN_CONTEXT snapshot carries only root, effective profiles, validated final directory mappings, active version and mode. Child path/version queries consume it after cwd/YAML/VERSION changes; explicit other-project selection discards it. Missing/invalid context fails clearly rather than rediscovering a root.
Preview retains an existing dev version, or uses dev1 from a release, without changing VERSION. Production uses the requested incremented release version from before hooks through rendering; success leaves dev1 of that release for subsequent development, and failure restores original bytes. Cache keys use v1.2.3-4 spelling; legacy version text APIs/files retain their accepted dotted representation. Final directory lookup remains unchanged in this slice; safe logical routing, render-context representation and native execution/embedding are subsequent work. Old-version renderer staging remains a known gap until the routing slice.



Safe output/data/docs-class lookup uses the selected eligible cache-class mapping, the captured active version and exact configured label. Final lookup preserves the physical mapping, including external paths. The later R-package data section defines the bounded output-r-data built-in; other generated labels must be declared. Directory insertion order is retained through configuration merging and the child snapshot. File fragments are relative and cannot replace/escape the role root. Queries never create directories. The CLI now defaults to safe lookup, integrated with captured-version consumers. Preview safe artifacts remain inspectable in cache and are not promoted.


Within directories, one cache-class mapping with boolean safe: true selects the safe cache. Otherwise an eligible exact cache label wins, then the first eligible cache-class mapping in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. Overrides retain existing key positions. Multiple explicit selections, non-boolean flags, flags on non-cache roles, or all declared caches excluded are validation errors before build mutations. A genuinely cache-free operation remains valid without any cache mapping. The effective selected label is frozen with the run context; children do not recompute it from subsequently changed YAML.
Legacy R data is package-generated output, not a generic input role. Its replacement/legacy normalization belongs to the separate output-r-data slice; this cache-selection change does not silently rename existing mappings.




Auto/absolute/relative are independent of safe/final target and execution cwd. Known managed renderer children receive an explicit bounded descriptor; no suffix or cwd-marker heuristics. Ordinary auto is caller-relative at query time; renderer auto is absolute. Relative bases are caller/project/known document/absolute custom directory. Explicit relative is strict across roots/drives; auto may fall back to absolute. Project renders without a single document reject document-relative base. The CLI now defaults to auto/safe. Merged settings may change representation, and explicit query flags override those defaults. Existing R helper/direct IDE parity remains unimplemented and outside Rust M1.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev use merged settings.execution-directory, falling back to native; explicit --execution-dir overrides the configured policy. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.



This source slice wires output consumers to the captured active version and selected eligible cache; CLI lookup defaults are now safe/auto. settings is runtime policy, build selects actions, and parameters remain analytical data. settings.output-clear-stage is none (default), pre or post. Explicit --output-clear-stage wins over merged settings, then legacy build.clear_output YAML, then PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT, then none. Legacy environment/build never means none. Canonical settings uses none only; invalid values, explicit null and unsupported settings fail in their source layer. This deliberately changes R’s production fallback pre; R has no settings section.
After read-only validation/recovery setup, start hooks run first. Other preparation (ignore metadata, renderer staging and fresh native artifact isolation) follows. Pre-clear is immediately before analysis; post-clear is immediately after successful analysis, before restoration/staging/promotion/hooks. These clear configured final output/data roots, never the versioned cache and never preview final destinations. Output actions disabled by output_run:false also skip final-output clearing. An empty analysis selection remains upload-only and skips analysis-related clearing. Docs finalization is a separate fresh-document operation, not ordinary output clearing.
Fresh renderer artifacts are copied to selected-cache/projr/v/docs in previews and releases. Individual render source location is preserved for native resource semantics. Versioned cache files remain inspectable; failed renderer scratch is retained there too. Generic safe output trees are copied to configured final destinations only on release, respecting final-output clearing policy. Unrelated existing final files remain under none. No cache is synthesized. Unused cache-free script operations remain valid; a safe path query without eligible cache fails. Automatic old-cache removal is rejected for production until it has a bounded policy.
Local finalization completes before end hooks, which immediately precede the next development-version bump. With configured irreversible storage/Git publication, record the successful local release version first, then publish, then end hooks and next-dev bump. Publication/end-hook failure after this boundary preserves the local release and reports partial finalization; remote actions cannot be rolled back. Without publication, end-hook failure remains inside managed recovery. Preview never publishes or bumps VERSION. Arbitrary script effects/concurrent writers/power loss are outside the managed recovery guarantee; this is no sandbox or M2 provenance.
PR159 review amendments freeze selected renderer paths and prepared project metadata, revalidate immediately before each renderer, isolate its native artifacts at that boundary, and collect only the frozen outputs. Controlled VERSION, ignore and renderer-metadata writes share immediate path revalidation; promotion rejects links and special files. Notebook invocation retains native rmarkdown intermediate naming. An exact per-worktree Git record permits only the framework-created unstaged next-development VERSION change at the same committed HEAD; other dirty state still fails. Added remote regressions and real notebook acceptance await the amended-head CI and independent re-review. These checks do not establish concurrent-writer or power-loss atomicity.



Individual Quarto HTML/revealjs and R Markdown html_document/html_notebook rendering defaults to resource embedding only when the document leaves the effective option unspecified. Explicit false remains respected; embed-sources is a separate option. External metadata for individual rendering remains unsupported under the existing layout restrictions.
Quarto project preparation uses native quarto inspect results for each effective document format. Only an HTML/revealjs format with neither embed-resources nor legacy self-contained specified receives a temporary document-header default. Quarto owns profile, included-metadata, directory and document precedence. Both spellings of explicit false remain untouched, including mixed documents. Original source and project bytes are restored exactly on success/failure, before promotion. Prepared-source changes or a changed native input set fail at the launch boundary; automatic project fallback requires modeled text documents. Other input types need explicit renderer embedding settings. No literal Markdown/LaTeX resource rewriting or R helper/IDE parity follows. Nonembedded portability remains deferred.
The native Bookdown render_site driver is unchanged and has no new embedding fallback in this bounded slice; combined M1 acceptance must record that limitation. Remote exact-head evidence and independent review are required before shipment.



This supersedes earlier blanket requirements for declared data-class labels: output-r-data is the canonical built-in R-package data lookup, with fixed final target project/data even without YAML. Safe lookup derives /projr//output-r-data and requires an eligible declared cache and valid version. Lookup never creates or activates this role.
Only an explicit directories.output-r-data: {} declaration or normalized legacy data declaration activates managed cleanup, recovery, promotion and explicitly configured publication. Use ordinary output rules: none preserves other final files, pre/post clears at the configured lifecycle stage, preview never promotes, and supported failure restores final bytes. No special preservation policy applies. Ordinary ignore rules apply; explicit ignore: [] includes data in Git/R builds.
Normalize legacy _projr.yml and active _projr-*.yml aliases before profile/local merging; reject same-layer conflicts and any redirection in each original layer. Normalize legacy remote content labels too. Canonical _proj.yml rejects data; generic data-* labels are unsupported (use raw-* inputs or output-* outputs). Existing R helpers/packages remain untouched. Python/Julia outputs use ordinary mappings; inst is a project-relative fragment, not a special role.
Embedding preparation preserves the complete native effective format list/order, including an inherited non-HTML default. Only eligible HTML options change. Prepared sources use guarded same-directory replacement with original permissions, so hard-linked external aliases retain their original bytes. Inherited renderer profile/directory/included metadata is captured and rechecked at launch; changes are rejected rather than silently masked by a prepared default. Internal captured metadata is recovered; external metadata is observed only and is never rewritten. Literal metadata-files paths are required for this bounded dependency capture.



The existing managed-renderer contract must hold across successive builds: failed HTML/PDF artifacts cannot enter a later successful Git commit after selecting fewer documents. Restore prior final/native bytes on failure; preserve unselected native documents and retained failed cache scratch across the retry. Successful document finalization still replaces the configured final docs tree with its new selection. No new attempt identity, sealing, cache namespace or storage policy is introduced. The remote mixed_render_retry.py acceptance exercises this sequence with real renderers and actual committed bytes; M2 record design remains open.



Ordinary proj use must remain standalone with a native backend and no DVC dependency. Future per-directory DVC backing is opt-in, with automatic delegation at agreed lifecycle points and DVC authoritative for its own tracking/cache. The intended release catalogue is a curated linear main-branch changelog. Storage design constraints separate these decisions from the still-open configuration, identity, sealing, manifest and backend contracts. This records design only; current runtime behavior is unchanged.



Real temporary Git repositories and a bare upstream now exercise the existing optional-publication contract: configured non-main/differently named upstream, explicitly disabled push, no-op provider commits, non-fast-forward rejection and an analysis-failure comparison. Check actual branch refs, committed/final/cache bytes and release/development versions. This adds acceptance evidence; current branch and publication order stay unchanged. Durable publication records, sealing and the future release catalogue are not implemented by these tests.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
Script and hook subprocesses inherit invocation cwd by default, retaining explicit selected input paths. Quarto and individual R Markdown retain native execution directory settings. Explicit --execution-dir project passes the captured root via supported renderer controls. Input/mode/root remain data arguments to fixed R code. Nested Quarto project metadata is rejected for selected documents and conservatively scanned implicit source trees. clear_output accepts only pre, post, or never; directory ignore accepts all, git, rbuild (case-insensitive), or an empty list. Invalid values fail before analysis, ignore synchronization or cleanup, including direct cleanup APIs.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
Ingestion requires an existing directory, disjoint from its CAS storage and project index. Reject linked/unsupported source entries, non-UTF-8 filenames and ambiguous logical paths; logical identities use slash-separated components and case-sensitive names. Digests are canonical 64-character lowercase hexadecimal BLAKE3 values. Copy and hash the same stream; verify existing objects before reuse. Publish complete objects/manifests without replacing conflicting content. Replace project index bytes through a same-directory temporary file, escaping CSV metadata fields.
Manifest inspection validates structure and manifest byte identity; file inspection also hashes referenced object bytes. This does not provide a stable snapshot across concurrent source changes, multi-writer serialization, power-loss durability or one transaction across remote manifest and project index. Failure may leave valid orphan objects or an unindexed complete manifest; errors propagate and old index bytes stay intact. No source file is modified by ingestion. Symlink-alias paths remain unsupported under the conservative path guards; callers should supply resolved physical paths.

title: Project and execution behavior
text: Git commits, pushes and network/upstream checks default off even when Git metadata exists. Only the resolved configured actions execute. Commit-enabled builds require clean initial Git state to avoid sweeping in unrelated edits; no-op commits succeed. Push captures the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference before build writes. Missing upstream and unmodeled custom push-only routing fail early. Native authentication is the default. An explicit token-helper opt-in uses fixed host-scoped code and ephemeral environment data, never secret argv/source or persistent credentials. Local build success remains distinct from publication failure.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
Preview captures managed root files/config/VERSION, selected inputs, declared output/docs trees, configured local publication stores and ordinary VCS metadata. Restore exact captured bytes/presence on both success and failure; restoration failure makes preview fail and reports retained recovery data when available. Declared cache is disposable and excluded from recovery; preview/cache artifacts remain there. No Git/publication operations execute in preview.
Recovery uses private temporary storage outside project cache. Unsafe linked or overlapping recovery paths fail before analysis; file-based/worktree VCS pointers are unsupported for this bounded metadata guarantee. This does not redirect arbitrary script writes, protect undeclared/external effects, prevent concurrent reads of temporary modifications, or provide sandbox/crash/concurrent-writer atomicity. New unmanaged files are not a whole-project snapshot. Automatic preview output isolation remains separate from post-run captured-state preservation.

title: Project and execution behavior

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
One effective profile list is selected before config/environment reads: CLI, nonempty PROJR_PROFILE, nonempty QUARTO_PROFILE fallback, then base/local build.profile default. Earlier profiles still win; local config is highest. A profile’s own build.profile does not redirect an already selected run. Native QUARTO_PROFILE rendering settings remain distinct; no R helper bridge follows. The private per-run PROJ_RUN_CONTEXT snapshot carries only root, effective profiles, validated final directory mappings, active version and mode. Child path/version queries consume it after cwd/YAML/VERSION changes; explicit other-project selection discards it. Missing/invalid context fails clearly rather than rediscovering a root.
Preview retains an existing dev version, or uses dev1 from a release, without changing VERSION. Production uses the requested incremented release version from before hooks through rendering; success leaves dev1 of that release for subsequent development, and failure restores original bytes. Cache keys use v1.2.3-4 spelling; legacy version text APIs/files retain their accepted dotted representation. Final directory lookup remains unchanged in this slice; safe logical routing, render-context representation and native execution/embedding are subsequent work. Old-version renderer staging remains a known gap until the routing slice.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
Safe output/data/docs-class lookup uses the selected eligible cache-class mapping, the captured active version and exact configured label. Final lookup preserves the physical mapping, including external paths. The later R-package data section defines the bounded output-r-data built-in; other generated labels must be declared. Directory insertion order is retained through configuration merging and the child snapshot. File fragments are relative and cannot replace/escape the role root. Queries never create directories. The CLI now defaults to safe lookup, integrated with captured-version consumers. Preview safe artifacts remain inspectable in cache and are not promoted.


Within directories, one cache-class mapping with boolean safe: true selects the safe cache. Otherwise an eligible exact cache label wins, then the first eligible cache-class mapping in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. Overrides retain existing key positions. Multiple explicit selections, non-boolean flags, flags on non-cache roles, or all declared caches excluded are validation errors before build mutations. A genuinely cache-free operation remains valid without any cache mapping. The effective selected label is frozen with the run context; children do not recompute it from subsequently changed YAML.
Legacy R data is package-generated output, not a generic input role. Its replacement/legacy normalization belongs to the separate output-r-data slice; this cache-selection change does not silently rename existing mappings.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
Auto/absolute/relative are independent of safe/final target and execution cwd. Known managed renderer children receive an explicit bounded descriptor; no suffix or cwd-marker heuristics. Ordinary auto is caller-relative at query time; renderer auto is absolute. Relative bases are caller/project/known document/absolute custom directory. Explicit relative is strict across roots/drives; auto may fall back to absolute. Project renders without a single document reject document-relative base. The CLI now defaults to auto/safe. Merged settings may change representation, and explicit query flags override those defaults. Existing R helper/direct IDE parity remains unimplemented and outside Rust M1.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev use merged settings.execution-directory, falling back to native; explicit --execution-dir overrides the configured policy. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.

title: Project and execution behavior
text:
This source slice wires output consumers to the captured active version and selected eligible cache; CLI lookup defaults are now safe/auto. settings is runtime policy, build selects actions, and parameters remain analytical data. settings.output-clear-stage is none (default), pre or post. Explicit --output-clear-stage wins over merged settings, then legacy build.clear_output YAML, then PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT, then none. Legacy environment/build never means none. Canonical settings uses none only; invalid values, explicit null and unsupported settings fail in their source layer. This deliberately changes R’s production fallback pre; R has no settings section.
After read-only validation/recovery setup, start hooks run first. Other preparation (ignore metadata, renderer staging and fresh native artifact isolation) follows. Pre-clear is immediately before analysis; post-clear is immediately after successful analysis, before restoration/staging/promotion/hooks. These clear configured final output/data roots, never the versioned cache and never preview final destinations. Output actions disabled by output_run:false also skip final-output clearing. An empty analysis selection remains upload-only and skips analysis-related clearing. Docs finalization is a separate fresh-document operation, not ordinary output clearing.
Fresh renderer artifacts are copied to selected-cache/projr/v/docs in previews and releases. Individual render source location is preserved for native resource semantics. Versioned cache files remain inspectable; failed renderer scratch is retained there too. Generic safe output trees are copied to configured final destinations only on release, respecting final-output clearing policy. Unrelated existing final files remain under none. No cache is synthesized. Unused cache-free script operations remain valid; a safe path query without eligible cache fails. Automatic old-cache removal is rejected for production until it has a bounded policy.
Local finalization completes before end hooks, which immediately precede the next development-version bump. With configured irreversible storage/Git publication, record the successful local release version first, then publish, then end hooks and next-dev bump. Publication/end-hook failure after this boundary preserves the local release and reports partial finalization; remote actions cannot be rolled back. Without publication, end-hook failure remains inside managed recovery. Preview never publishes or bumps VERSION. Arbitrary script effects/concurrent writers/power loss are outside the managed recovery guarantee; this is no sandbox or M2 provenance.
PR159 review amendments freeze selected renderer paths and prepared project metadata, revalidate immediately before each renderer, isolate its native artifacts at that boundary, and collect only the frozen outputs. Controlled VERSION, ignore and renderer-metadata writes share immediate path revalidation; promotion rejects links and special files. Notebook invocation retains native rmarkdown intermediate naming. An exact per-worktree Git record permits only the framework-created unstaged next-development VERSION change at the same committed HEAD; other dirty state still fails. Internal captured metadata is recovered; external metadata is observed only and is never rewritten. Literal metadata-files paths are required for this bounded dependency capture.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Standalone ordinary use
proj must work with its own native backend without installing DVC. DVC must not become the mandatory manifest engine or a dependency of ordinary proj use. Existing interpreter and renderer requirements still apply to selected analyses.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
Optional DVC-backed directories
Future integration may let users opt individual directories into DVC backing. Only users selecting that integration need DVC. proj should automatically delegate the appropriate operations at the agreed lifecycle points.
proj retains its logical directory labels/roles and path abstraction regardless of backend. Integration must preserve label resolution so analysis code does not depend on DVC-specific physical paths.
DVC remains authoritative for its own tracking and cache state. proj references the corresponding versions rather than maintaining a second authoritative copy of DVC’s data/cache inventory. Projects should be able to mix native and DVC-backed directories. Missing DVC, unavailable data and delegation failures need explicit handling; proj must not silently install DVC.
The directory configuration, supported restore/build/store operations, exact hook timing and failure/recovery boundaries still need design. This note does not adopt old command recipes or decide a provider contract.

title: Storage and release catalogue design
text:
A curated release catalogue
The intended release catalogue is a curated, linear history on the main branch, presented as a readable changelog. A general catalogue of every run on every branch is not the product goal. This direction does not change current build or Git branch policies, or remove the need to report failed attempts honestly.
Attempt/release identity, allocation, sealing and how failures relate to this catalogue remain open. So do the manifest schema, durable storage, remote-only discovery, retention and Git-tracking policy. No M2 persistence implementation or milestone completion follows from these constraints.
See the behavior contract, current lifecycle and compatibility log for implemented behavior and limits.

title: Build execution flow
text:
This describes the current Rust implementation, not a complete correctness or reproducibility guarantee. The behavior contract records approved semantics and the compatibility log records evidence and gaps.


Capture the project root, resolve a private per-run environment without changing the parent process, require active root configuration, and merge base/profile/local settings. Validate fields, explicit directory paths, targets, hooks and destructive destinations. Explicit empty scripts select no analysis. Otherwise explicit globs or shallow root discovery select inputs; project rendering may use its own input discovery. Explicit Python-only selection does not activate an unused Quarto/Bookdown project marker.
Read VERSION with DESCRIPTION/default fallbacks. Check selected interpreters and configured Git restrictions before controlled project writes. Existing preflight can still invoke Git/network checks or R package remediation; these are known limitations, not a clean-environment guarantee.



Before authoritative writes, capture exact bytes, permissions and presence/absence for the managed set documented in the compatibility log. This includes VERSION, ignore/configuration files, existing root regular files, selected in-project inputs, declared output/docs trees and planned individual rendering artifacts. External declared output/docs directories are allowed. Linked managed trees are rejected. Backups stream into private OS temporary storage outside disposable project cache. Backup creation failure prevents authoritative project writes.
One local error/panic boundary covers ignore synchronization, requested pre-cleanup, pre/both hooks, script/document execution, renderer configuration, promotion and post/both hooks. Required output promotion errors propagate. Renderer configuration is restored exactly, retaining comments and originally absent keys. Candidate version changes stay in memory; VERSION is written only after those stages succeed. No pre-build Git commit is created.
On local failure, restore the captured managed set, including originally absent files/directories. Attempt all restorations; retain recovery backups and report both the primary and restoration errors when recovery fails. Storage export and Git publication start after successful local completion. Export actual declared content before requested clear_output: post cleanup. Create one configured final Git commit, then push when enabled. A publication or later cleanup failure reports that local analysis succeeded and retains its release/version; external publication is not rolled back.
Git upstream/authentication policy, stable attempt/release records and an analysis-free publication retry command remain unfinished. Push uses the captured current-branch upstream; custom push-only routing remains unsupported and fails before authoritative writes. Native authentication is the default.



Previews skip production version changes, cleanup, commits and exports. They run selected hooks/analysis and restore captured managed state after success and failure, while cache output remains. Scripts still choose preview output locations; this is not automatic output redirection or an OS sandbox. Script/hook subprocesses start with the captured invocation cwd by default. Only an explicit project execution mode passes Quarto an execution-directory override; individual R Markdown receives a non-null knit_root_dir only in project mode. Direct R/IDE parity remains unfinished and is not established by these CLI controls. The existing R package remains untouched.

Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. title: Configuration _proj.yml
text:
The _proj.yml file dictates the structural map of your project. It configures the foundational paths and mapping logic used by the CLI.


Custom directory labels are strictly validated against a set of foundational prefixes: - cache - raw - output - docs
These prefixes are case-insensitive. Any label defined in the configuration must begin with one of these approved identifiers.



Ordinary declared directories need a nonempty path. The fixed R-package role output-r-data: {} is the exception: its final destination is project/data. Runtime does not insert other missing cache/raw/output/docs mappings or synthesize subpaths for undeclared labels. Canonical data/data-* labels are rejected; see the R-package data section for the legacy per-layer data alias. For example, declaring raw-data: {path: _raw_data} makes raw-data available; it does not create an undeclared raw or raw-data-extra resource. ASCII case is ignored and case-only duplicate labels are rejected.
proj --project . --non-interactive init directories creates a missing _proj.yml once with explicit raw-data: _raw_data, cache: _tmp, and output: _output paths. It preserves existing base/profile files, creates only declared resource directories, and does not invoke Git/GitHub or add an R code directory. The preset omits build.scripts, preserving shallow discovery; it never serializes an accidental empty analysis list. To render documents, declare a docs mapping too.
Production state and project-render staging require a declared cache directory. Framework version/staging children are derived inside that declared cache; this is distinct from inventing undeclared resource labels. Storage content labels must be declared and relative storage paths use the captured project root.



Each cache-class directory may include boolean safe. One explicit safe: true selects that cache; otherwise an eligible exact cache label wins, then the first eligible cache in merged declaration order. safe: false excludes a candidate. Profile/local overrides retain existing declaration positions. For example:
directories:
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  cache-analysis:
    path: _analysis_cache
    safe: true
This selects _analysis_cache for explicit safe logical output lookup. Multiple true selections, non-boolean values (including null), selection flags on non-cache roles, and all declared cache candidates excluded are validation errors. Each layer’s explicit values are checked before merging; null cannot inherit a previous boolean. Cache-free queries and operations that do not consume a cache remain valid. The chosen safe cache is frozen in child run context. Cleanup, safe lookup and renderer staging consume that same selected mapping; no literal cache label is required when another eligible cache is selected.



The system performs strict validation on _proj.yml: - If a defined directory label uses an unsupported prefix layout, a validation error string will be returned and execution will fail. - All references must resolve correctly; otherwise, the CLI will output an error detailing the structurally invalid labels or malformed content.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level config block for project-wide settings:

config.git.engine: The Git execution engine to use. Can be auto (default) or system. This determines how the CLI interfaces with Git capabilities natively.
config.git.use_proj_cred_helper: Defaults to false: use existing native Git authentication. Explicit true permits an existing single-line GITHUB_PAT, GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN for standard HTTPS github.com remotes through a temporary host-scoped helper. There is no automatic token discovery or GitHub CLI call during builds. Tokens are environment data, never argv or shell source; persistent auth settings are unchanged.




The _proj.yml file supports a top-level parameters block for arbitrary nested parameter evaluation. This allows you to define custom metadata and deeply queried values throughout your execution environment.
The configuration engine also supports several aliases for this block: parameter, params, and param. However, multiple alias conflicts within the same configuration file are structurally rejected during validation to prevent mapping confusion.



The _proj.yml file supports a top-level remotes block, which currently supports a local mapping of standalone storage vaults.

local: A mapping where keys represent remote titles and values configure the vault:

path: The physical absolute or relative path to the remote storage directory.
structure: Specifies the storage structure algorithm. Must be cas (Content-Addressable Storage).
content: An array of string tags (matching foundational prefixes or defined directories) specifying which project output directories to sync into the remote upon build completion.
inspect: manifest validates JSON, logical paths/digests and manifest filename/content identity; file additionally hashes every referenced object and compares actual bytes. Manifest-only inspection does not verify object bytes.





The _proj.yml file can also contain a build block to configure the behavior of the proj build and proj build-dev execution engine. The build block supports the following sub-keys:

dest: An optional list of remote target strings. These targets must be mapped to explicit configurations within the remotes.local block. During post-build execution, resolved content directories matching these tags are piped to the CAS engine for deduplicated storage synchronization.
scripts: An optional list of explicit script paths or glob patterns to execute during the build pipeline.

Globbing patterns are supported.
Prefix a pattern with ! to exclude matching files from execution.
Current source rejects malformed inclusion or exclusion syntax before execution, including hook patterns. The exclusion correction is newer than preview.2; see the build reference.
When provided, this selects scripts instead of automatic discovery. Document targets may be grouped for rendering, so mixed script and document targets are not guaranteed to run in the exact listed order.

hooks: An optional map of lifecycle hook scripts to execute.

pre: Scripts executed before the actual build phase.
post: Scripts executed after analysis/promotion, before VERSION and publication.
both: Scripts executed during both pre and post phases.

profile: An optional environment profile identifier. When set, the system injects the PROJR_PROFILE environment variable into the isolated subprocess for all executed scripts and project rendering commands. This can be overridden at runtime via the --profile CLI flag.
git: An optional Git integration configuration. This can be a boolean toggle or an object mapping out detailed toggles:

commit: Defaults to false, including inside an existing Git repository. Explicit true requires initially clean Git state and commits once after successful local build; an unchanged staged index is a successful no-op.
push: Defaults to false. Explicit true publishes HEAD to the current branch’s configured upstream remote/reference. Missing upstream or custom push-only routing fails before build writes; origin/main is never invented.

restrictions: Configuration block to enforce Git checks specifically during production builds:

only_branches: A list of allowed branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is not in this list.
not_branches: A list of restricted branch names. Production builds will abort if the current branch is in this list.
not_behind: Omitted/false performs no fetch. Explicit true fetches the current configured upstream and compares its state. If enabled, production builds will verify that the local branch has an upstream tracking remote and is not behind it, aborting if the local branch needs to pull upstream changes.

clear_output: An optional string controlling workspace clearing routines for output directories. Can be set to "pre", "post", or "never". If omitted, defaults to evaluating the PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT environment variable.




You can define a dev block to completely override specific configurations during development builds (proj build-dev).

scripts: A list of script paths or globs. During development builds, this array entirely overrides build.scripts. An explicitly empty array ([]) selects no analysis scripts. An absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts. Hooks can still run.
hooks: A mapping identical to build.hooks. When specified, these completely replace build.hooks during a development build.
old_dev_remove: Retained configuration field. The current preview protections skip CLI cleanup of prior caches during development builds, even when this is true. Scripts and hooks still control their own writes.





PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL: During the proj build pre-flight checks, if required R packages (like bookdown or rmarkdown) are missing, this environment variable controls remediation. If set to true, packages are automatically installed. If absent or set to false, the tool defaults to an interactive terminal prompt (if available) or fails hard.




build declares actions; settings controls how they run. Parameters are analysis inputs, not execution controls. This is an intentional extension beyond projr.
settings:
  output-clear-stage: none
  execution-directory: native
  path-representation: auto
Use none to preserve other existing final files, pre to clear immediately before analysis, or post to clear immediately after successful analysis and before output promotion/finalization. Preview never clears released outputs. Pre-hooks run before pre-clear; end hooks run after finalization immediately before the next-dev bump. The command’s explicit –output-clear-stage overrides merged settings; those override legacy build.clear_output, then PROJR_CLEAR_OUTPUT, then the new none default. Legacy never is accepted in the legacy field/environment. The canonical settings key accepts only none/pre/post, with invalid values/null rejected before merge or mutation. execution-directory accepts native/project; explicit --execution-dir wins over merged settings, then native is the fallback. Native scripts inherit launch cwd; native document execution remains renderer-defined. path-representation accepts auto/absolute/relative; explicit path-query --format wins over merged settings, then auto is the fallback. Auto is caller-relative ordinarily and absolute in a known managed renderer. Both settings reject null, booleans and unknown values in each active file before merging. Managed child queries retain the captured representation policy even if scripts change configuration, profiles or cwd. Safe is the default path target; final must be explicitly requested. Docs output handling and the R-data built-in remain separately modeled features.



The built-in output-r-data lookup has fixed final destination project/data, even without YAML. Querying never activates build management or creates directories. Safe lookup needs the selected declared cache and active version.
To opt into ordinary output clearing and success-only promotion:
directories:
  cache:
    path: _tmp
  output-r-data:
    ignore: []
An empty output-r-data mapping also activates the role, with ordinary default ignore rules. Explicit ignore: [] includes package data in Git and R builds. The path may be omitted; if present it must resolve to project/data. Redirection is forbidden. settings.output-clear-stage applies normally: pre/post clears old package data; the default none preserves other final files. Preview never promotes final data.
Legacy _projr.yml and active _projr-*.yml layers accept data as an alias and normalize it before merging, including legacy remote content labels. Defining both aliases in one layer is an error. Canonical _proj.yml requires output-r-data. Generic data-* labels are unsupported; use raw-* inputs or ordinary output-* mappings.

title: proj build
text:
The build pipeline script execution engine for the project.
This command evaluates what files need to be run based on configuration layout parameters (build.scripts in _proj.yml) or filesystem auto-discovery. It sorts them according to strict engine precedence rules, modifies format-specific configuration templates when necessary, and executes each script inside its own independent, isolated subprocess.



--major, --minor, --patch: Specifies the version bump strategy for a production build.
--profile: An optional profile to configure execution context.
--description: An optional description string for the build commit. If omitted during a production build that involves git commits, the CLI will interactively prompt for a one-line description when running inside a valid terminal session.





Pre-flight Dependency Checks: Before modifying files or triggering git snapshots, the build engine statically resolves targets to identify dependencies. Depending on the matched scripts (such as .Rmd, .qmd, or .py) and configuration files, it asserts the availability of Rscript (verifying required R namespaces like rmarkdown or bookdown), quarto, or python executable commands. Any missing R packages can be resolved automatically via the PROJR_AUTO_INSTALL environment variable, or through an interactive terminal prompt.
Production Build Restrictions: Checks if branch rules (only_branches, not_branches) or upstream synchronicity (not_behind) are violated during a production build run.
Remote Export Pipeline: During the post-build phase, conditionally exports resolved local target outputs into a deduplicated Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) vault as defined via build.dest targets in remotes.local.
System Git Provider Abstracted: Git mutations safely resolve through a strictly encapsulated host System Git adapter, securely avoiding hanging inputs and ensuring older systems correctly push mutations.
Mutual Exclusion Checking: Before executing, proj build checks for project-level configurations (_quarto.yml and _bookdown.yml). If both exist and the build targets include Quarto or RMarkdown documents, it throws an error to prevent conflicting rendering.
Explicit Execution (Path A):

Define exact scripts, exclusions (starting with !), or sub-directory globs in _proj.yml under build.scripts.
Can rewrite _quarto.yml or _bookdown.yml configuration if specific subset documents are requested.
Maintains order relative to Python and R scripts, while correctly clustering and executing project documents together.

Fallback Execution (Path B):

If no build.scripts is provided, the engine auto-discovers build targets.
Will execute a Quarto project if _quarto.yml exists, or a Bookdown project if _bookdown.yml exists.
Otherwise, it falls back to a shallow workspace sweep and runs .qmd, .Rmd, .R, and .py files in that strict order.





Every resolved file or project rendering task runs inside its own completely independent subprocess, isolated via environment profiles (PROJR_PROFILE) and correct working directory assignments (current_dir), preventing memory leaks and state pollution across execution runs.



proj build-dev
Development runs execute the existing script selection with development Git settings disabled. The CLI does not create or update VERSION, update ignore files, clear released output or previous caches, promote rendered documents into docs, or export to configured local archives. These rules apply on success and failure, even when production configuration enables cleanup, commits or export.
Scripts should explicitly write preview artefacts into their declared cache or staging locations. A subprocess is not a filesystem sandbox: scripts, hooks and renderers can still write where their own code/configuration directs them. Renderer configuration rewriting and script working-directory behavior retain their existing semantics. This change does not introduce automatic output redirection, recursive discovery or a new project-root policy.



build.scripts: [] selects no analysis scripts. Hooks still run, and production builds can version and export existing artefacts as an upload-only workflow. Analysis cleanup, renderer setup and document promotion are skipped so those existing artefacts are preserved. The CLI does not discover scripts instead.
For previews, an absent dev.scripts inherits build.scripts; dev.scripts: [] overrides it with no analysis. Hooks still run, but previews never publish.



Builds require root-level _proj.yml, legacy _projr.yml, or an explicitly activated _projr-<profile>.yml. Inactive profiles and _projr-local.yml alone do not qualify. Both base filenames together are an error. Unsupported control fields fail before build writes; arbitrary parameters and metadata maps are allowed. Configuration errors include their causes on stderr and return failure.
This validation is separate from project discovery. A root marker or cwd fallback does not make an unconfigured project buildable. Explicit directory enforcement, per-run environment isolation and complete managed-state failure restoration remain under development; see the behavior contract and pinned legacy audit.
Explicit script/hook include patterns must match at least one file. Use an empty list (scripts: []) when intentionally selecting no analysis; unmatched configured includes return an error instead of a successful no-op.
Current source reports directory-enumeration and entry-inspection errors instead of treating a failed fallback scan as an empty selection. Errors name whether fallback discovery or managed-state capture failed and retain the OS cause. The sweep stays shallow, alphabetically ordered within each language, and skips linked entries; hidden and Git-ignored regular scripts remain eligible. This diagnostic correction is newer than preview.2, whose permission failure may appear later as a bare OS error.
Current source also validates every script/hook exclusion pattern before hooks, analysis, clearing or controlled build writes. A malformed pattern such as ![[ fails with a nonzero structured error instead of silently running excluded code. This includes exclusion-only lists and post/both hook selections. Valid exclusions retain include order and first-match deduplication; an exclusion need not match a file. This correction is newer than the published preview.2 binary, which can silently ignore malformed exclusions. Check exclusion syntax before using that installed preview; the source fix does not update it automatically.
Native execution policy (supersedes earlier unconditional root-cwd wording): build and build-dev default to --execution-dir native. Plain scripts/hooks inherit the invocation cwd, not each source file’s parent; R source() normally inherits its caller cwd. Individual Rmd rendering leaves knit_root_dir unset and Quarto receives no execution-dir override, preserving native document/project settings. --execution-dir project explicitly requests captured-root execution for scripts/hooks, Quarto and individual Rmd. Project render drivers run from the selected project root to select the project, independently of chunk cwd. Project-wide Bookdown root override is currently rejected early because its render_site entrypoint does not expose the individual knit-root argument. Captured project/profile/version and logical path identity do not change with execution cwd. No existing R helper bridge or literal Markdown resource rewriting is implied.



Individual Quarto HTML and R Markdown HTML default to embedding resources when unspecified. An explicit format option of embed-resources: false (Quarto) or self_contained: false (R Markdown) is respected. Quarto project defaults use native effective-format inspection, including profiles, directory and included metadata. Only formats leaving both embed-resources and legacy self-contained unspecified receive temporary header settings; original source bytes are restored exactly. Changing a prepared source/input set before rendering is rejected. Other project input types need explicit embedding settings. embed-sources controls source attachment and is unrelated to resource embedding.
Source documents keep their original paths and bytes. Literal Markdown/LaTeX references retain native meaning. Linked output may still depend on its source tree; nonembedded relocation is not supported by this change. Existing restrictions on inherited metadata for individual rendering remain in force. Bookdown site rendering retains its native resource policy and has no new fallback here.
See Quarto HTML embedding and R Markdown render options.
Project embedding preparation keeps native format choices and their order, even when a non-HTML format is the default. Original permissions and external hard-link bytes are preserved. Changing inherited profile/directory/included metadata after preparation is rejected; use literal metadata-files paths. External metadata is read for validation and is not rewritten. Arbitrary external script effects remain outside managed recovery.



Managed renderer failure restores the previous released documents and original native artifacts before a later build can commit. A successful smaller document selection publishes that selection; it replaces the previous final docs tree. Unselected earlier native documents stay unchanged. Failed renderer scratch is retained under the declared versioned cache for inspection, separate from final documents. Cache is disposable and should remain ignored by Git.
The remote acceptance driver tests real individual and project Quarto HTML/PDF renders, a deliberate later-document failure, then a smaller successful local Git build. It compares committed report bytes with both final and cached files, checks the entire commit for failed report artifacts, and preserves retained failed scratch. This adds acceptance coverage to the existing lifecycle, not a new retry identity or transaction guarantee. It does not update installed preview.2 or complete M2 provenance.



Git commits and pushes are separate opt-in actions. A push uses the current branch’s configured upstream, including a differently named remote branch; it must not silently target main. Disabling push still allows a local build commit. The real-repository tests verify both settings against a temporary bare upstream and compare the committed and published CSV bytes.
If Git rejects a push after local analysis and commit succeed, the command fails and reports that the local release is preserved. Its files, local release commit and release VERSION remain available; the next-development bump is skipped. An analysis failure instead restores the previous managed state and creates no release commit. Neither outcome implies a remote transaction or a durable publication record. Do not automatically rerun analysis to retry a failed upload.
No-op commit behavior is tested at the Git provider boundary: unchanged files produce no extra commit, while a real change does. A normal production CLI build advances VERSION and therefore need not be a no-op.

text:
Successful CLI commands return exit status zero. Reported operation failures return a nonzero status and a diagnostic on stderr, including configuration/path queries, version reads/writes, ignore updates and initialization. Argument parsing errors also return nonzero.
For example, a malformed _proj.yml makes proj yml read --project demo fail, so a shell or frontend can stop instead of treating the diagnostic as success. Failed Git staging, commits and GitHub creation propagate as initialization errors; a failed remote inspection does not proceed to GitHub creation.
This defines success versus failure, not stable error codes, a JSON result schema or a capability protocol. Diagnostics remain human-readable text. Commands may perform work before failing; a nonzero status is not a rollback guarantee.

Independent static review, 2026-10-20. Baseline: 41bd7000363f34b1e7e2d7e354971bfe9021e2b1 (relevant implementation blobs also match 5617a6daed1f4743a9b2609694a2f84ad4c902eb). Finding and baseline source
Required correction and evidence




Overlapping docs/output/cache paths; docs . or ancestor; symlinked parents; separator-bearing labels. yml.rs:337, clear.rs:158, fs_utils.rs:1.
Reject unsafe destructive destinations before writes; resolve identity/overlap and staging aliases; protect source/raw/root state. External resource paths remain valid. Test actual preservation with root/ancestor/overlap/traversal/symlink fixtures.


VERSION and outputs change before hooks; rollback covers only the execution middle. build.rs:236, build.rs:328.
Stage managed writes and cover hooks, snapshots, execution, postprocessing and promotion with complete error handling. Restore exact prior managed state, including VERSION absence/bytes.


Public docs cleared before ignored promotion failures; post-cleanup precedes CAS export. build.rs:359, build.rs:370, build.rs:430.
Require successful expected-output promotion and archive real output bytes before cleanup; never report success after failed/missing promotion. Preserve the previous release on failure.


Environment read errors suppressed through lines().flatten(); invalid names can panic; required files can be ignored. env.rs:69, env.rs:181.
Bounded reads, validation before mutation, explicit errors for directory/unreadable/empty/NUL inputs; prove analysis never starts.


Environment guard mutates process-wide variables across library builds. env.rs:118.
Resolve a per-run map and apply child-command environment explicitly. Overlapping projects must not exchange variables/profiles/credentials or change caller environment. A private mutex cannot protect unrelated readers.


Credential helper embeds tokens in arguments/shell text, ignores requested host and inherited-helper behavior. git.rs:146.
Prefer native configured authentication. Any override needs fixed code, exact host scope and no secret in argv/source. Use synthetic punctuation-bearing sentinels and mocked Git; never real credentials in logs.


Optional Git work runs implicitly; fetch despite disabled checks, duplicate commits, hardcoded branch and discarded token. build_pre.rs:112, build.rs final Git stages.
Execute only requested operations using real upstream/native auth; handle clean commits and separate local success from publication failure. Mock Git/network tests.

Required correction and evidence

Validate early; prefer supported renderer controls, otherwise exact-byte restoration on every exit.


Individual documents ignore configured docs destination; PDF/DOCX formats guessed as HTML; promotion errors discarded. build.rs:271, build.rs:363, build_pre.rs:79.
One validated destination and explicit supported format mapping; reject unsupported formats rather than guessing; require actual expected artifacts.


Rmd filename interpolated into executable R source. build.rs:990.
Pass data/arguments to fixed R code; test spaces, apostrophes, backslashes and Unicode without local R execution.


Remote paths stay invocation-relative and invalid content tags/errors are dropped. yml.rs:429, build.rs:435.

title: Machine interface
text:
Machine interface
Use proj --machine <command> for automation. Human command output remains the default. proj capabilities (also with --machine) reports protocol/capability versions and supported command families without loading a project.
Protocol version 1 writes one JSON object and a newline to stdout. Both success and failure include protocol_version, cli_version, ok, result, and error. result is null on failure; error is null on success. Failures exit nonzero. Broken output pipes cannot receive a complete object and also exit nonzero.
proj --machine capabilities
proj --machine --project . path get --label output
proj --machine --project . version get
proj --machine --project . yml read
proj --machine --project . build-dev
Successful queries return { "path": "..." }, { "version": { "major": 1, "minor": 2, "patch": 3, "dev": 0 }, "text": "v1.2.3" }, or { "validated": true }. Configuration queries validate without returning raw configuration or parameter values. Other existing command families reuse the ordinary CLI in a noninteractive subprocess and return { "completed": true } only when that command succeeds. Unsupported command arguments fail; capability flags explicitly report absent preview isolation, attempt/release records and direct R/IDE parity.
Stable error codes are invalid_arguments, project_selection_failed, query_failed, command_failed, and worker_unavailable. Messages are static; raw config, environment values, command arguments and chained domain errors are not copied into protocol errors. This transport reuses existing anyhow domain handling tracked by issue87; it does not promise a finer domain-error taxonomy. With --machine, help/version display requests return capability negotiation.
All command progress and child stdout/stderr go to stderr, streamed directly without accumulating logs in memory. Machine mode closes child stdin and enables noninteractive policy. Child logs are user/third-party output and are not a secret redaction service; avoid printing credentials in scripts. No environment/config dump is included in the machine result. Callers must keep stdout and stderr separate.
A failed publication can follow successful local analysis. command_failed is not a rollback or retry instruction: inspect local state/diagnostics before retrying. No analysis-free publication retry or successful release record is invented here.
